chk_problem.reason: Both drafts identify the same core problem of investigating whether reasoning models' internal representations encode relative long-horizon candidate value for next-token choices.

chk_method.reason: Both drafts describe the same method of using sparse linear probes on hidden states, MLP outputs, and attention outputs.

chk_data.reason: Both drafts identify the Reasoning Candidate-Token Value (RCTV) dataset as the dataset used.

chk_setup.reason: Both drafts describe the experimental setup involving the same three models (Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-8B, and DS-Llama-3.1-8B).

chk_primary_result.reason: Both drafts report the exact same primary result of a 4.30 percentage point improvement in continuation accuracy at a budget of 64.

chk_secondary_result.reason: Draft A focuses on generalization to other models and entropy regimes, whereas Draft B focuses on outperforming baseline models in AUC metrics.

chk_baseline.reason: Both drafts list the same set of baselines, including uniform random, probability, rank, and embedding-based baselines.

chk_conclusion.reason: Both drafts conclude that internal representations encode relative long-horizon candidate value and that this can be linked to or used to improve reasoning outcomes.

chk_limitation.reason: Both drafts identify the limitation of focusing primarily on mathematical reasoning problems.
